newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak arms maker splits to attract fresh money.
newsitem.headline: Slovak arms maker splits to attract fresh money.

text.p: Slovak arms maker ZTS TEES Martin a.s., as part of a plan to become more streamline and attract new capital, has split into four wholly-owned subsidiaries, the Economics Ministry said on Thursday.

Peter Dudak, director of the ministry's specialised production department, told Reuters on Thursday the four daughter firms would remain under the control of ZTS, while the state will keep its veto right on strategic decisions.
"The plan is to have clean firms with better preconditions for finding loans on the money market," Dudak said.
"Negotiations with the ministry on a solution for ZTS's problems have been going on for some time," added Jozef Skrko, a senior ZTS TEES oficial.
The ministry expects the new companies, which have already been officially registered, to begin full operation in August, Dudak said.

The subsidiaries are: ZTS TEES Martinske strojarne a.s., to specialise in the production of tractors and engines, ZTS TEES VOS a.s., a machine tool maker, ZTS TEES Lesne traktory a.s., producer of heavy-duty tractors and ZTS TEES Energetika a.s., which makes power generation products.
Dudak said the basic production programme of ZTS TEES itself would remain unaffected by the move.
"They (the new firms) will continue their current activities, but it will be neccessary later to reconsider whether these are profitable or not," he said.

ZTS TEES, which also produces the modernised version of the Soviet designed T-72 M tank, is part of the state-run holding company DMD Holding a.s. founded in 1996 to coordinate the production and export of the country's 26 arms producers.
"DMD Holding's representatives will sit on supervisory boards of the new companies to ensure a common strategy," Dudak said.

Historically among the Warsaw Pact's chief armourers, Slovak arms sales and production have dwindled by more than 90 percent from their level before the fall of communism in 1989. The workforce in the whole sector was reduced to some 18,000 people from 80,000 in the mid-80s.

ZTS TEES, which was badly affected by the halting of arms production and a subsequent conversion programme introduced in 1990, faces the need to reduce its workforce currently of some 4,400 -- a sensitive issue in economically depressed central Slovakia.
"So far we have only reduced working hours without planning organisational changes," Skrko said.

Added Dudak: "There is general over-employment in the engineering industry compared with low productivity in the sector. They may avoid huge dismissals, but they must definitely change the make-up of the workforce."
